notes: Route that works: https://www.emol.com/sitemap/sitemapIndex.xml (HTTP 200) lists per-year shards /sitemap/xml/sitemapN_YYYY.xml (8 of them for 2026, each HTTP 200, flat <urlset>, NO <lastmod>). The publication date comes from the /YYYY/MM/DD/ segment of the article path /noticias/<Section>/YYYY/MM/DD/<id>/<slug>.html; on 23 re-fetched articles the page's own <meta property="article:published_time"> equalled that path date (two were one day later, i.e. inside the 1-day tolerance). Earlier attempts failed for one reason only: every <loc> in the sitemap is http://www.emol.com/... and plain HTTP does not answer at all (connection error -> polite_fetch status 0, 0 bytes, which is exactly the status 0 / 0 chars in the previous sample report), while HTTPS answers 200 with ~120 KB pages. So the scraper rewrites every URL to https://www.emol.com. Also: non-existent shards (sitemap8_2026.xml, sitemap9_2026.xml, sitemap10_2026.xml, sitemap12_2026.xml) answer with a dropped connection (status 0), not 404, so only the shards named in the index are fetched; one retry per shard guards against a transient loss of ~1000 URLs. Tried and rejected: /sitemap/xml/sitemap{n}_2026.xml probing beyond the index (no files, status 0), and http scheme in general. Result: 2572 unique https URLs over all 31 days of 2026-09-25..2026-10-25, 2026-09-30 = 109, 2026-10-10 = 49, 2026-10-20 = 99, minimum day 2026-10-25 = 24. Verified by re-fetching 16 articles sampled across all 8 sections: all HTTP 200, 2983-11461 chars of extracted text, page date equal to the listed date (16/16 good; the previous 0/6 came purely from the http scheme). Run time 45-90 s, all requests through polite_fetch.
